q1212: Journaling = a log of changes that lets a filesystem recover to a consistent state after a crash.
q1213: Automating ticket workflows = consistent handling with less human error.
q1214: Duplicate, concurrent requests exploiting missing synchronization = race condition.
q1215: Phishing-resistant MFA = security keys (FIDO2) and passwordless. Codes by SMS, email or IM can be phished.
q1216: Strong signature algorithm = proves who signed (authenticity) and that nothing changed (integrity).
q1217: 'Technical defense' against phishing = a secure email gateway filtering mail before users see it.
q1218: Several providers send your mail and it lands in spam → add every sender to the SPF record.
q1219: SIEM collects over SSH with nothing installed on the server = agentless.
q1220: Malicious code slipped into legitimate vendor updates = supply chain attack.
q1221: Warm site = the balance between cost and recovery time.
q1222: Estimate how often an asset stays up (availability) = MTBF.
q1223: Keep a third party's assessment results confidential, legally binding = NDA.
q1224: Salting defeats rainbow tables (precomputed hashes). Key stretching adds rounds.
q1225: Static website defaced → FIM detects file changes + WAF blocks the attack requests.
q1226: Tailgating through badged doors = a social engineering weakness (people, not locks).
q1227: TPM = hardware chip that stores keys securely and performs crypto functions.
q1228: Telling staff when they may apply updates = change management (scheduled, communicated changes).
q1229: Same secure settings on every cloud instance = a reusable template (IaC).
q1230: CAB rejects a technically complete change → the rollback (backout) plan is missing.
q1231: Tracking logins and time spent = accounting (the third A in AAA).
q1232: Integrity of compiled binaries in production = code signing.
q1233: ACL = preventive (blocks before it happens). SIEM, cameras, honeypots = detective.
q1234: Phishing aimed at the CEO or other top executives = whaling.
q1235: Where did the data go? → NetFlow sorted by destination IP.
q1236: One external developer builds all your critical software = vendor lock-in.
q1237: Passive recon = public sources and normal connections only; no payloads or fuzzing.

q1239: Make code hard to reverse engineer to protect IP = obfuscation.
